source.title: Batch Group Normalization
source.authors: Xiao-Yun Zhou; Jia-Cheng Sun; Nan-Yang Ye; Xu Lan; Qijun Luo; Bolin Lai; P. Esperança; Guang-Zhong Yang; Zhen-Guo Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares normalization methods and reports classification accuracy, but does not measure training classification error or test whether gradient training reaches near-zero training error. Its BN discussion of training degradation concerns validation accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation accuracy, not training classification error. These results do not test the claim versions. It also cites prior work about normalization and training, which is not this study's own result.
record.test_reason: The study uses normalization in vision models and evaluates its proposed BGN method against other normalization methods. Its own results report final validation accuracy and some convergence failures, without testing any claim version. In particular, V6 requires accuracy gain over training or learning-rate tolerance; comparisons of final accuracy between normalization methods do not establish either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that BGN provides good performance, batch-size stability and generalizability, and can complement other methods. Their broader assertion of consistent superiority needs qualification: BGN slightly underperforms BN in MANAS and ties it on one Office-31 task.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes and evaluates Batch Group Normalization against other normalization layers; the experiments compare validation accuracy and do not test the claim's training-error outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: BGN's validation accuracy varies with batch size and group number G; the paper reports different G settings across batch sizes and tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet ResNet-50 validation accuracy with BGN exceeds BN at every tested batch size: 77.008% versus 76.832% at 128 images per worker, and 76.096% versus 66.512% at two.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BGN improves final ImageNet validation accuracy over BN in the tested recipes, especially at small batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, DARTS validation accuracy is 97.40% with BGN versus 97.33% with BN; MANAS accuracy is 97.15% versus 97.18%. IN and LN fail to converge in both experiments, and PN also fails in MANAS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice affects convergence and final validation accuracy in the tested NAS architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: In adversarial training, BGN achieves 49.64% robust and 72.94% clean validation accuracy versus BN's 48.79% and 72.09%; PN fails to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BGN improves final robust and clean validation accuracy over the converged normalization baselines in this adversarial-training setup.

fits_no_version.finding: On miniImageNet, BGN achieves 59.50% one-shot and 76.32% five-shot accuracy versus BN's 59.30% and 76.22%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BGN yields slightly higher reported few-shot accuracy than BN in the tested setup.

fits_no_version.finding: On Office-31, BGN has the highest reported mean adaptation accuracy, 90.9%, versus BN's 90.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BGN improves mean domain-adaptation accuracy over the listed normalization methods in the tested setup.

record.problems: No training classification-error results are reported for the claim. The reported classification comparisons use validation accuracy; the ImageNet accuracy is described as the median over the last five epochs, but no uncertainty intervals are given for those comparisons. Few-shot results report 95% confidence intervals, and Office-31 results are averaged over three runs.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: reported outcomes concern validation accuracy or convergence in downstream vision tasks rather than a claim-version measure of training classification error or the specified training dynamics.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels, and dependence on size, stopping time or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Effects of initialization on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Accuracy gain during training and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN; training speed and stability with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche were inconsistent. T4 fits its use of normalization and evaluation of a proposed method. The exclusion rationale should address each version's actual outcome: training classification error is central to V1 and V3, while V6 concerns training speed and learning-rate tolerance. The reported convergence failures do not establish those comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error; CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 fit from random initialization, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration effects.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth changes, and the effects of special initialization or removing normalization.
Initialization effects on training speed, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Training loss and curvature behavior above or near a learning-rate stability threshold.
Accuracy gain during training and learning-rate tolerance for otherwise matched networks with and without batch normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
